items.title: Japanese Yen futures post strongest session since October 22.
items.excerpt: Japanese Yen futures recorded their strongest daily percentage gain since Oct. 22, climbing 0.77% to trade near the session high of 63.23 after touching a low of 62.67. The advance put the yen on pace for its first positive week in four, accounting for nearly all of the 0.77% weekly gain. In economic data, Japan's October headline inflation rose to 2.3% year over year from 2.1%, while core inflation printed at 2.2% against expectations of 2.3%. Following the softer core reading, market-implied probability of a 25 bps Bank of Japan rate hike in December eased to 77% from 87%. A pullback in technology and AI equities also prompted safe-haven flows into the yen and the Swiss franc as the U.S. dollar came under pressure.

Meanwhile, the CME Group Volatility Index (CVOL) for the euro remained relatively steady across the past two sessions while holding above weekly lows. Market pricing continues to reflect expectations for December rate hikes from both central banks.

items.title: British Pound futures slide as UK inflation trails forecasts.
items.excerpt: British Pound futures fell for the sixth session in the last seven, dropping 2.13% over that stretch to reach their lowest level in nearly a year. During the session, the contract recorded a high of 1.3210 and a low of 1.3136 before finishing the New York cash session down 0.48%. The downward move followed October UK inflation data that came in below the Bank of England forecast ahead of its Dec. 17 policy decision. Headline CPI rose to 3.6% year over year from 3.5%, trailing the central bank projection of 3.73%, while services inflation held at 3.7% and core inflation remained at 2.8%. UK labor market figures also showed signs of cooling as regular pay growth slowed to 3.5% from 3.7% in the three months through September. items.title: Euro futures close below 1.10 at new year-to-date low.
items.excerpt: Euro futures extended their decline to close below the 1.10 level, marking a new year-to-date low and falling more than 2% since last week. The downward momentum initially began alongside a firmer U.S. dollar as market expectations around interest rate hikes shifted, before accelerating in recent sessions. As the euro moved lower, implied volatility tracked by the CME Group CVOL index continued to climb higher. Meanwhile, positioning data from last week revealed that speculators exited their net short positions rather than adding to them, marking the largest positioning reversal since the summer.
